New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith was scheduled to be a full participant at practice Friday and appears on track to start against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday (4:05 p.m. ET on FOX).

Smith twice left the Jets’ 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills last Sunday, first to be evaluated for a head injury late in the first half and then after he hurt his left ankle during his only series of the third quarter. He was limited at practice earlier this week, but said Wednesday he intends to play.

"He'll be practicing fully today, so we'll see how that goes," coach Aaron Glenn said before practice Friday. "He looks solid. It's very encouraging."

The Jets (2-8) are looking to snap a five-game losing streak when they face the Chargers (1-8), who got their first win when they beat the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night.

Smith was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik last week. The fourth-round pick from Clemson would make his first NFL start if Smith can’t go, but that doesn't appear to be the case this week.

Glenn said the team would see how Smith, left guard Dylan Parham (knee), defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) get through practice Friday before making final calls on their availability for the game at Los Angeles.

"We've got two days to see how these guys operate," Glenn said. "It is looking promising for all these guys, so I feel good about that."

The offense will be down two wide receivers, though, with Glenn ruling out rookie Omar Cooper Jr. with ankle and hip injuries and Isaiah Williams with a rib injury. Neither was expected to practice Friday after sitting out the other practice sessions this week. Both were hurt against Buffalo.

The Jets have Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Tim Patrick and rookie Malik McClain as healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Sterling Shepard and Jamaal Pritchett are on the practice squad. Tight ends Mason Taylor and rookie Kenyon Sadiq could also see increased targets in the passing game.

"I think that's the good thing about the tight end room is those guys can actually end up playing some of those receiver spots that we have," Glenn said.

Williams is the Jets' primary punt returner, so Isaiah Davis could assume that role. Williams also shares kickoff duties with Kene Nwangwu.

Defensive lineman David Onyemata, on injured reserve the past eight weeks with an abdominal injury, won't be activated from injured reserve this week, Glenn said. The Jets opened Onyemata's 21-day practice window on Wednesday, so they have two more weeks before they need to either activate him or place him on season-ending IR.

text:
Star Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered one of the most unfortunate injuries of the NFL season when he tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye early in the Lions' win over the Pats in Munich, Germany.

Hutchinson brought Maye to the ground and then jumped into the air in celebration. He tore his knee when he landed.

Hutchinson is out for the remainder of the season, dealing a significant blow to the Lions' hopes of making a run through the playoffs. On Thursday, Hutchinson released a statement about the injury, his recovery and his future celebration plans via his Instagram account.

"I honestly can't believe it. I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me," Hutchinson wrote. "But even something like this won't hold me back."

In the wake of the injury, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said that he's retiring his backflip celebration because of what happened to Hutchinson. And now, Hutchinson himself says he won't be jumping in the air in celebration anymore, either.

"Two things I know for sure: 1. I always come back stronger," Hutchinson said. "2. That's the last time I go airborne 😁👍"

Hutchinson getting injured while celebrating his sack meant that he joined a sneakily extensive list of players suffering unusually-timed injuries, such as Lamarr Houston, Stephen Tulloch and Bill Gramatica, each of whom also tore their ACL while celebrating a play.

Hutchinson's injury probably won't stop everyone in the league from celebrating in the air, but if it inspires even a few more players to stop going airborne, that'll probably be for the best.

Dan Campbell won't tell his players to stop celebrating

For what it's worth, Lions coach Dan Campbell said that even in the wake of Hutchinson being lost for the season, he won't tell his players to stop celebrating on the field.

"I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say, 'Nobody celebrates anymore,'" Campbell said on 97.1 The Ticket.

Campbell also recalled a story from his own playing days while again stating that he won't tell players to stop celebrating their on-field accomplishments.

"No, I don't believe that. I think what happened speaks for itself," Campbell said. "We're not talking to 8-year-olds here. And I'll give you a story. I remember one time I made a big play, and I freaking pumped my arm up and I'm pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn't tell anybody. I was just excited. I just pumped my arm.

"This game is built off of emotion. And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I'm not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you gotta keep your head — then you're really becoming something you're not."

Campbell is a firm believer in building the personality of your team. It's clear that he doesn't want to change his team's personality — which has been built in his own image over the years — even in the wake of a devastating injury.

text:
Cardinals fans may be holding their breath going into the weekend over whether Carson Beck will be able to play on Sunday against the Chiefs.

Beck was placed on the Cardinals’ injury report on Thursday as a limited participant due to a back issue, raising concerns about whether he will be available for the Week 11 game, which would reignite the quarterback shuffle that Arizona has gone through this season.

The rookie quarterback had been dealing with back spasms a few weeks ago, according to Cardinals reporter Dani Surreck.

Arizona Republic Cardinals reporter Theo Mackie noted in a post on X that Beck had been in the team locker room after practice and “seemed to be walking around normally.”

An update on Beck’s status will take place on Friday when the team releases its final injury report of the week.

While Beck’s stat line didn’t appear to be anything special, reviews of his first NFL start — a 34-6 loss to the Rams — were more complimentary.

He finished completing 11 of 18 pass attempts for 108 yards and had two interceptions.

“I think the overall operation of our offense was really good,” Beck told reporters after his first game. “That’s something that [head] coach [Mike] LaFleur talks about a lot is the operation [and] getting in and out of the huddle. There were a couple communication things that [for] the first time being out there — calling plays again in a live game and live action and just getting better, being more clear and concise with the huddle, being able to get in and out quickly and get on the ball and snap it right.

“Everything that you can control before the ball is actually snapped and there are live bullets flying, but I think that was good. Just going where the defense told me to go, reading the defense, reading out our plays and trying to give guys opportunities to make plays. For me as a quarterback, that’s what I’m here to do. Run the offense, have great operation, get in and out of the huddle and then ultimately play clean football. I think that’s something that this offense can do.”

If Beck isn’t able to go on Sunday, Josh Johnson and Joey Aguilar are the Cardinals’ backup options.

Today is a big day if you are a video game player. Grand Theft Auto VI, perhaps the most anticipated video game in history, has been released. A huge part of the anticipation is that it was 13 years between the release of GTA V and GTA VI. Which made us wonder, what was the Miami Dolphins’ roster when GTA V was released on September 17, 2013?

The Dolphins just finished a game at the Indianapolis Colts when GTA V was released - coincidentally Miami is also coming off a game at the Colts as GTA VI is released. In that 2013 game Miami won 24-20, giving them a 2-0 start to the season. They would finish the year 8-8 and in third place in the AFC East.

text:
The Denver Broncos are getting healthier as the practice week progresses.

Coming off their bye, the Broncos are close to full strength, not counting the handful of players on injured reserve, some of whom they'll be getting back in the next few weeks.

Things are looking good on the health front for the Broncos, and they're still buzzing over the Riley Moss extension, but things are also improving for the Las Vegas Raiders. Let's take a look at how Thursday's practice report shook out for both teams.

Broncos' Thursday Practice Report

Jaylen Waddle | WR (Concussion)

Kris Abrams-Draine | CB (Ankle)

Zach Allen | DL (NIR-Rest)

Courtland Sutton | WR (NIR-Rest)

Analysis

Everyone but Jones was a full participant on Thursday, including Abrams-Draine, who was limited on Wednesday. Jones remains limited, but given that he's had nearly three weeks to bounce back from his hamstring injury, there's a good chance he'll play on Sunday, even if he ends up listed as questionable on the final injury report.

But that's me putting an optimistic spin on things. The Broncos have been without Hufanga for the past four games, so just getting him back will be great for the defense, but having him and Jones patrolling the back end will be just what the doctor ordered.

Lohner continues to practice in full after the Broncos started his clock to return from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list on Wednesday. It's unclear when the Broncos plan to make a decision on Lohner, but it could come before Sunday's game.

If Lohner gets activated, though, the Broncos will need to make room on the 53-man roster, and they already have four tight ends. With each practice Lohner has, there are a handful of guys at the bottom of the roster who get a little more uncomfortable.

Allen and Sutton returned to full participation, too, though they're limited designation on Wednesday was for rest only, as the Broncos ease them back into the swing of things after the bye. If Jones can progress on Friday, all the health stars will be aligned for Denver.

The Raiders have been trying out kickers this week with Gay's injury, but the real story on Thursday was Bowers's return to practice. The star tight end suffered a "significant" injury on Sunday against Seattle, and did not return in the second half.

Bowers didn't participate on Wednesday, but he was back out there on Thursday, albeit in limited form. Sources close to the Raiders indicate he's very focused on trying to play this game against the Broncos, so despite the early signs this week being unfavorable, it's too soon to count him out.

The Raiders are dealing with some injuries on their defensive line, as you can see, so it'll be interesting to see how Fatukasi and Hemingway progress on Friday.

text:
The Arizona Cardinals have added quarterback Carson Beck to the injury report, a potentially concerning development ahead of their Week 11 trip to face the Kansas City Chiefs.

Beck was officially listed as limited for practice on Thursday, Nov. 19, with a back injury. He was later present in the locker room while it was open to reporters, and appeared to be walking around without discomfort. The injury report was first released shortly after the locker room closed to reporters.

This is not the first time Beck has had back trouble this season, as he dealt with a back injury for two weeks in October. That injury first surfaced on Oct. 16. He missed two practices the following week and was listed as a limited participant three times, before returning to full participation on Oct. 29. Until now, he had not been listed on the injury report since then.

“He’s just dealing with a bit of spasms,” head coach Mike LaFleur said on Oct. 23, of Beck’s previous injury. “It’s not like a long-term (issue) or anything like that. But trying to throw the way these guys throw, if you’re having a little bit of a back tweak, that’s what’s going on with him.”

LaFleur’s next press conference is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, two days before the Cardinals’ game against the Chiefs in Kansas City.

If Beck’s injury were to force him out of the game, the Cardinals would likely turn to veteran journeyman Josh Johnson, who served as their backup last week. Johnson was signed by the Cardinals on Nov. 10, along with Joey Aguilar, who was the third-string emergency quarterback last week.

The bigger concern, though, would be the impact on Beck’s development, after an encouraging NFL debut in last week’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. (AP) If ever there was a time for an NFL team to overlook somebody, it just might be Sunday afternoon at Arrowhead Stadium, where the Kansas City Chiefs will continue their pursuit of another AFC West title against the injured, downtrodden Arizona Cardinals.

The Chiefs (7-2) have moved back into first place in the division thanks to tiebreakers over the Broncos, who have an identical record through the first nine games. But a slip-up against the Cardinals (3-7) could be downright disastrous considering the Chiefs are staring at a five-week meatgrinder that includes the likes of first-place Buffalo, Cincinnati and San Francisco.

“They've had a lot of injuries, obviously, but they still have a lot of NFL talent on the roster,” Chiefs linebacker Drue Tranquill said. “At this point, the message is just about us stacking wins in November and December, and we're going to try to do that on Sunday.”

The Chiefs have bounced back nicely from back-to-back losses in Seattle and Denver, taking advantage of what was long perceived to be the soft part of their schedule. They blew out the Jets 35-12 at home a couple of weeks ago, and they beat the Falcons by an almost identical 35-13 score last week - their fifth win by at least two touchdowns this season.

Even without ailing running back Kenneth Walker, and injuries along their offensive line, the Chiefs have been able to score at a high clip. Patrick Mahomes is playing like an MVP again, throwing five touchdown passes last week in Atlanta, and the acquisition of wide receiver Josh Downs in a trade with Indianapolis is already paying dividends for Kansas City.

Its defense has been stingy, too, holding Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson in check last week.

Juxtapose that with the Cardinals, who were waylaid 34-6 by the Rams last weekend.

Arizona put safety Andrew Wingard and linebacker Jordan Burch on injured reserve this week, pushing their total to 16 players on injured lists, tied with the 49ers for most in the NFL. That includes quarterback Gardner Minshew II, first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, fellow running back Trey Benson, wide receiver Michael Wilson and offensive tackle Paris Johnson II.

The injury to Minshew means that Carson Beck will make his second consecutive start this week. The third-round pick out of Miami endured a rough NFL baptism last weekend, going 11 of 18 for 108 yards with two interceptions against the Rams.

“It’s us coming up with the best plan possible to put these guys in position to be successful, and then them going and executing the job," Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said. "Every single guy, if you ask them - if they have a jersey and they’re in the National Football League, they’re going to tell you they belong, and they’re going to tell you that they can make the plays.

"They have another opportunity this week to get that done.”

Arizona (3-7) at Kansas City (7-2)

When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, CBS.

Latest odds: Chiefs by 15 1/2.

Against the spread: Cardinals 4-6, Chiefs 5-4.

Last week: Cardinals lost to Rams 34-6; Chiefs beat Falcons 35-13.

Last meeting: Chiefs beat Cardinals 44-21 on Sept. 11, 2022.

Series record: Chiefs lead 10-3-1.

Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson against the Cardinals run defense, which allows 129.9 yards per game, fifth worst in the NFL.

Walker is expected to miss his second game because of a groin injury, which means the fifth-round pick out of Nebraska will once again be the featured back. Johnson filled in on short notice last week in Atlanta, running for 101 yards and catching six passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns. He has 519 yards from scrimmage this season, second most among all rookies.

The Cardinals, meanwhile, have allowed at least 120 yards rushing in six of their 10 games, and they were especially bad against the Rams. Blake Corum ran for 100 yards, Ronnie Rivers ran for 81, and the Rams finished with 202 yards rushing as a team.

- The Chiefs have won five of the past six in the seldom-played series. They are 4-0 against the Cardinals at Arrowhead Stadium.

- Chiefs TE Travis Kelce has caught a pass in 200 straight games, the longest streak in franchise history and the longest active streak in the NFL. The longest streak by a tight end in NFL history is 211, set by Tony Gonzalez.

- Downs had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs debut in Atlanta. The Chiefs acquired him for a pair of draft picks from Indianapolis early last week, and he should be more comfortable with a full week of practice this week.

- Chiefs WRs Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong each caught their first career touchdown pass against the Falcons. Allen's was from 39 yards and Armstrong's was from 43.

text:
In his first public comments since suffering a torn ACL sustained while leaping into the air to celebrate a sack of Patriots quarterback Drake May, Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson vowed to “come back stronger” and never “go airborne” again in an Instagram post on Thursday, Nov. 19.

Four days after Hutchinson’s season was ended by a celebration gone wrong during the team’s 35-10 win over New England in Munich, Germany, Hutchinson let the fanbase hear from him and addressed blowback about his decision to sky into the air in celebration, which resulted in his knee buckling underneath him.

Similar celebrations have taken out several players since the turn of the century, including an infamous local instance in which Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch was lost for the remainder of the 2014 season.

“I honestly can’t believe it,” Hutchinson began. “I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me.

“But even something like this won’t hold me back.

“I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why, and I always trust him.

“Very grateful for your prayers and well wishes,” Hutchinson said.

Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown said on his podcast, “St. Brown Bros,” earlier this week that he and Hutchinson, along with running back Jahmyr Gibbs, all practiced the celebration, used by many pro soccer players over in Europe, after Saturday’s practice at the FC Bayern Munich Campus.

Across the league and among fans, Hutchinson drew considerable criticism for continuing to do a celebration that had taken out several NFL players, specifically an ex-Lion.

Hutchinson is also known for a move popularized by soccer legend Cristiano Ronaldo, the “Suiii,” where he leaps into the air, spins 180 degrees, then lands and explosively thrusts his arms out. In a video posted by the Lions’ social media team after a sack against the New Orleans Saints in the season opener, Hutchinson does the move, and many fans begged him to stop.

“Two things I know for sure:,” Hutchinson’s statement continued.

1. I always come back stronger.

2. That’s the last time I go airborne,” Hutchinson said, concluding his second note with a smiling emoji and a thumbs up.

“Hold down the fort til I’m back, boys,” he finished.

It’s the second time in three seasons that Hutchinson has suffered a season-ending injury. In 2024, he missed the final 12 games of a season in which Detroit went 15-2 because of a broken tibia and fibula.

With the win against New England, Detroit (7-2) moved into first place in the NFC North, but will find themselves with the difficult task of surviving without All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell, who’s out indefinitely with a neck injury that occurred on Nov. 1, and Hutchinson, one of the highest-paid defensive players in the NFL.

title: Puka Nacua's suspension exposes a far bigger NFL problem - 12th Man Rising
description:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua was suspended for three games by the NFL on Thursday, but he won't miss any games that he otherwise would have missed anyway.
This isn't about what Nacua allegedly did, but about the league not starting his suspension after his return from injured reserve.
The Rams could have suspended Nacua if the team thought its image suffered from whatever the wide receiver did, but that's not how the NFL works normally.
Still, a team missing a player already out with an injury shouldn't be able to benefit from the NFL having a concurrent suspension.
It looks as if the league doesn't really care about the matter and only hands out the suspension to appease public perception.
text:
Do not adjust your computer screens. What you are about to read about a player who plays for a Seattle Seahawks rival is true. Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua was suspended for three games by the NFL on Thursday, but he won't miss any games that he otherwise would have missed anyway.

The punishment for violating the league’s personal conduct policy, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, covers part of the period of time that Nacua is on injured reserve for a knee injury and turf toe. The only real punishment Nacua will face is financial, and therein lies the rub.

The NFL is implying that it cares more about money than about truly punishing those who might have done bad things away from the field. This isn't about what Nacua allegedly did, but about the league not starting his suspension after his return from injured reserve.

NFL's suspension of Puka Nacua doesn't have much teeth

The Rams certainly benefit from this weird rule because they will get their best receiver back in the same amount of time as they would have. Nacua's injury could keep him out longer than the minimum of four games he has to serve. Not that the team did this necessarily, but if there was any inkling that Nacua was going to be suspended, placing him on IR actually helped LA.

If the league really wanted to take a stance that it cared about what NFL employees did to others away from the football field, it wouldn't have a rule that allows a suspended player to serve time while on IR. That seems illogical.

The only real loss for Nacua is that he will miss the paychecks of those games he wouldn't have been playing while injured. His per-game salary is $320,389, so he will ultimately be fined $961,167. That might affect what Nacua does for dinner, but not much else.

The Rams could have suspended Nacua if the team thought its image suffered from whatever the wide receiver did, but that's not how the NFL works normally. The league is in charge of doling out punishment. The money that Puka Nacua gives up will go to charitable causes, so at least there is some good in that.

Still, a team missing a player already out with an injury shouldn't be able to benefit from the NFL having a concurrent suspension. The player gets to return when he normally would, and his life isn't changed much. The team is better off.

While the entire matter might simply have been collectively bargained over between players and the league, the truth is that everyone should care more about how the NFL looks when they suspend a player who wouldn't be playing in the first place. It looks as if the league doesn't really care about the matter and only hands out the suspension to appease public perception.

title: Sen. Blunt Rochester pushes NFL for blood clot policy after Hurts injury - WDEL
description: The blood clot injury that ended Eagles QB Jalen Hurts' season hit close to home for Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Delaware).
text:
The New Castle County Vocational Technical School District i…

Thanks to the generosity of WDEL's listeners and advertisers…



Congresswoman Lisa Blunt Rochester delivered her final scheduled address on the House floor as a member of the House Tuesday, December 17th

The blood clot injury that ended Eagles QB Jalen Hurts' season hit close to home for Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Delaware).

Blunt Rochester lost her husband Charles to a pulmonary embolism, when blood clots reached his heart, and she said when she learned of Hurts' injury "my stomach dropped."

According to the American Lung Association, pulmonary embolisms affect 1 in 1,000 people, and is the third-leading cause of heart-related death in the United States.

With that in mind, Blunt Rochester said she wrote to National Football League Commissioner Roger Goodell asking what policies were in place to protect players from situations like Hurts, who suffered blood clots during a game in London, and then flew back to the United States.

"This is a severe medical issue, and one that people need to take seriously," she said in a social media post on Thursday.

She said the NFL and the NFL Players Association will do a joint review with independent experts to see if they need to consider further league-wide policies on the topic.

title: Texans lose Chris Braswell to serious-looking knee injury - ESPN
authors: DJ Bien-Aime, Kevin Seifert, Bill Barnwell, NFL Nation, Jeremy Fowler, Dan Graziano, Jordan Reid, ESPN staff, John Keim, Nick Suss
description:
HOUSTON -- Texans defensive end Chris Braswell suffered a serious-looking knee injury on the opening kickoff of Thursday night's game against the Indianapolis Colts.
As the ball was being returned by the Colts, Braswell collided with Indianapolis defensive end Caden Curry and his leg buckled, sending him down to the ground immediately.
A medical cart came out for Braswell, and payers surrounded him while an air cast was placed on his right leg.
Thursday night was Braswell's first time playing in a Texans uniform after landing on their practice squad Sept. 1.
He was elevated to the active roster ahead of Thursday night's game.

DETROIT — Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson is speaking out after suffering a season-ending injury, sharing an emotional message with fans and teammates on Instagram.

Hutchinson was placed on injured reserve after tearing his ACL while celebrating a sack during the Lions’ Nov. 15 victory over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany.

He acknowledged the shock of the injury and said he’s determined to return stronger on Thursday (Nov. 19).

“I honestly can’t believe it. I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me,” Hutchinson wrote. “But even something like this won’t hold me back.”

The former Michigan Wolverines star also reflected on his faith, saying he is trying to accept the circumstances rather than question why the injury happened.

“I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why, and I trust in Him,” Hutchinson wrote.

“Two things I know for sure:

I always come back stronger.

That’s the last time I go airborne," Hutchinson wrote, adding a smiling emoji.

Hutchinson ended the message with encouragement for his teammates, writing: “Hold down the fort til I’m back, boys.”

Hutchinson’s injury leaves major hole for Lions

Hutchinson’s absence is a significant loss for Detroit’s defense, as he has established himself as one of the team’s most important defensive players.

The Lions will have to move forward without their star pass rusher while Hutchinson focuses on rehabilitation and recovery.

Despite the setback, Hutchinson’s message made one thing clear: He intends to return to the field and pick up where he left off.

text:
With the NFL playoff picture beginning to take shape, Week 11 brings a heavyweight showdown in Mexico City, a nightmare for fantasy football owners and some of the biggest betting spreads we’ve seen in years. Meanwhile, Joe Burrow is making a serious push for the season’s MVP and the injury-ravaged Lions say it’s next man up. Here are 5 things to know about Week 11.

Sunday night in CDMX

The NFL’s international slate wraps up Sunday, but don’t worry about setting an early alarm. The Vikings (7-2) and 49ers (8-1) will square off in primetime at Estadio Banorte (formerly called the Estadio Azteca) in Mexico City, marking the league’s sixth game in Mexico.

And both teams are going to extreme lengths to prepare for the altitude. San Francisco spent the week training at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, while Minnesota took a more high-tech approach, constructing a “high-altitude room” at its facility that simulates elevations up to 12,000 feet. Vikings players have logged nearly 450 sessions in the chamber over the past five weeks.

Kyle Shanahan already won one international preparation battle this season, arriving early in Australia before the 49ers hammered the Rams 27-7 in the opener. Will his strategy pay off again?

On the field, it’s a fascinating clash of strengths: Brian Flores’ defense ranks second in yards allowed, while the 49ers boast the NFL’s top-ranked offense. And with Kirk Cousins back under center, Minnesota has renewed confidence in its passing game.

Cousins could become the first quarterback to lead two different teams in touchdown passes in the same season. He threw 20 with the Raiders before returning to Minnesota, where he’s just four touchdowns away from overtaking Kyler Murray for the Vikings’ team lead.

“Byemaggedon” has arrived

Fantasy football owners, good luck setting your lineups this week. The dreaded “Byemaggedon” is here, with a season-high six teams taking the week off. The Falcons, Browns, Packers, Rams, Patriots and Seahawks can all rest up for Week 12.

That means plenty of fantasy stars will be unavailable at a critical point in the season, just as leagues enter the home stretch before the playoffs.

The NFL traditionally loads up on byes before Thanksgiving, when the schedule gets even more complicated. No teams will be off during Thanksgiving week, but the byes return in Week 13 with the Colts, Raiders, Giants and Ravens resting. The Cowboys and Cardinals will finally get their turn in Week 14.

Massive spreads, upsets to come?

Oddsmakers aren’t expecting much drama in several Week 11 matchups. A whopping five teams are favored by double digits, which, according to Action Network, would be the most such games through the first 11 weeks of an NFL season since 2009.

The Bills are 16.5-point favorites over the Dolphins, the Chiefs are laying 15.5, the Texans are favored by 12.5 over the Colts, the Bears are giving 11.5 and the Broncos are 10-point favorites over the Raiders.

But don’t pencil in those wins just yet. We’ve already seen two double-digit underdogs pull off outright upsets this season. The Cardinals stunned the Rams in Week 6 as 12.5-point underdogs, and the Giants knocked off the Texans in Week 7 despite entering as 10-point dogs.

With five opportunities for another massive upset, don’t be surprised if at least one favorite gets a rude awakening Sunday.

Burrow’s MVP march heads to DC

Can anyone slow down Joe Burrow right now? The Bengals quarterback has been absolutely surgical during Cincinnati’s five-game winning streak, throwing an eye-popping 20 touchdowns against just three interceptions.

After knocking off the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, Burrow and the Bengals are back in primetime for the second straight week, this time facing Dan Quinn’s Commanders on Monday night.

Burrow has surged to the front of the MVP conversation, and his numbers are approaching historic territory. He’s on pace for 51 touchdown passes, a total that would trail only Peyton Manning’s record-setting 55 in 2013.

The Bengals are rolling, Burrow is playing arguably the best football of his career, and another national television showcase gives him a chance to strengthen his MVP case.

Lions remain steadfast despite pain

The Lions just can’t catch a break. Detroit’s injury nightmare took another devastating turn last week when star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of Drake Maye. To make matters worse, Maye suffered a severe ankle injury on the same play.

Asked whether he would consider banning celebrations, Dan Campbell delivered a classic response: “We’re not talking to 8-year-olds here.”

But the injury has certainly gotten players’ attention around the league. Giants running back Cam Skattebo says he’s retiring his signature touchdown backflip after seeing what happened to Hutchinson.

For Detroit, the bigger concern is what happens next. The Lions had already lost standout linebacker Jack Campbell to a serious neck injury, leaving them without arguably their two most important defensive players.

That puts even more pressure on Detroit’s explosive offense to carry the load down the stretch. The Lions host the Buccaneers on Sunday.

text:
When Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson crumbled to the turf following a jump in the air, a natural follow-up question emerged: Should NFL players be more careful with their celebrations?

While the Lions are not outright banning expressions of jubilation, players themselves are free to make their own decisions.

And in New York, it appears one high-profile player decided to shelve his high-risk celebration.

Giants running back Cam Skattebo said Wednesday, Nov. 18, he is retiring his signature backflip after touchdowns in the wake of Hutchinson’s season-ending torn ACL.

“I’m done flipping, just for that reason,” said Skattebo, according to NJ.com, of Hutchinson's injury. “It’s hard to see. Don’t want it to happen to me. ...

“I’m serious. There’s no reason to flip. Mentally, I’m like: ‘[Expletive] it. I’m not doing that [expletive].’”

But like every story, there are two sides to this.

In a follow-up story Thursday by NJ.com's Darryl Slater, wide receivers Malachi Fields and Darnell Mooney said they aren't planning to stop their own back-flipping or any other celebrations.

“I think in the moment, if you’re feeling it, you’re going to do it regardless," Fields said. "You don’t think about that stuff in the moment.

“It’s just celebrating. I bet [Hutchinson] wasn’t even thinking. He was just celebrating. Just a crazy thing. Man, it’s insane. But you definitely don’t think about it in the moment.”

text:
The Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) look to record a third consecutive win when they take on the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.

Favored to win by double-digit odds, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid may rest some starters, particularly running back Kenneth Walker III, given the quick turnaround. Four days after hosting the Cardinals, the Chiefs get back on the road for a tough matchup against the Buffalo Bills (8-1) on Thanksgiving Day.

Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce reaggravated his ankle injury after a 23-yard catch-and-run on the opening drive against the Falcons, was a full participant in practice on Wednesday.

"I'm ready to rock and roll this week," Kelce said on the November 18 episode of his "New Heights" podcast.

"I love playing this game," he continued, "and if I'm out there on a good ankle or a bad ankle, it doesn't [expletive] matter to me. I'm out there because I love this game. I signed up for this thing to be out there putting my heart on the line and my body on the line for my teammates."

While Reid loves Kelce's drive, he also knows when to put the 37-year-old veteran in his place.

Chiefs Head Coach Andy Reid Doesn't Care If Travis Kelce Gets Mad, 'He's Not 20 Anymore'

Speaking to reporters about Kelce's status, Reid noted how Kelce "wanted to fight me" to get back into the game against the Falcons. With the Chiefs already well on their way to defeating Atlanta 35-13, Reid kept Kelce on the sidelines.

"He wants to play. He wants to practice every play. He wants to play every play," Reid said. "I want to make sure that thing doesn't get worse. "Unfortunately, that play," Reid noted of the tackle by Falcons safety DeMarcco Hellams, "the whole action of twisting probably wasn't real good for it.

"But He's doing well now. He's running around. High ankle sprains, he's had this before, and they get tweaked literally, and then they recover fairly quick from there. That's what this was. It just happened early in the game. He was very mad."

Overall, when it comes to Kelce managing his workload, Reid smiled and shook his head. "He thinks he's still 20."

Chiefs Star Travis Kelce Doesn't Think Demarcco Hellams Made a 'Dirty Tackle'

Kelce spoke about his injury scare on "New Heights," and addressed a fan's question on whether he thought Hellams mad an "intentionally dirty tackle."

Kelce answered, "I don't know if that was the case; the way he tackled me… I just got caught in a bad position. You know, that's football. And on the flip side, you know, if it was a quote-unquote intentional, you know, extra grab and turn of the ankle, you know, it's just part of it."

"I don't think it was, you know, crazy enough for it to get a flag or it to be a fine or anything like that," he added. "Obviously, in the moment, I thought it was, because it hurt like hell."

authors: Jordan Raanan, Jeff Legwold, Ian Rapoport, Adam Rittenberg, Seth Walder, Bill Barnwell, NFL Nation, Jeremy Fowler, Dan Graziano, Stephen Holder
description:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is retiring his trademark celebratory backflip for the time being.
This comes on the heels of Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson suffering a season-ending knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack Sunday.
Skattebo, the Giants starting running back, is coming off a serious ankle injury last year.

Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL while celebrating a made kick against the Giants in 2001.
text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is retiring his trademark celebratory backflip for the time being.

This comes on the heels of Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson suffering a season-ending knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack Sunday. Hutchinson was placed on injured reserve.

"It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Wednesday. "I'm saying, yeah, [no backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.'

"That s--- ain't going to happen to me."

Skattebo, the Giants starting running back, is coming off a serious ankle injury last year. But he returned for the start of the season and backflipped after scoring in New York's season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys. He backflipped as recently as Thursday night in a loss to the Washington Commanders.

Skattebo isn't saying he won't backflip again. The likelihood is he will. He has done it his whole life. But he mentioned after the opener that he might put the celebration on the backburner, before it reemerged in Week 10.

Skattebo conceded Wednesday the backflip might resurface "if we go to the playoffs or something."

The backflip was a point of contention throughout the offseason, even before Hutchinson had his mishap. Skattebo did his flip for the first time since the injury after hitting a home run at the Brian Burns Celebrity Softball Game in late May.

Skattebo then stumbled while doing a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the summer, creating a stir.

Giants brass had a conversation with Skattebo afterward. They preferred he didn't do it leading into the season, especially coming off a major injury. They didn't mandate he never do it again.

"The big-picture message is you want to take care of yourself, take care of your team. Do everything you can do to be healthy, be back, be right, be good," Giants coach John Harbaugh said at the start of training camp. "What does that mean? It's not going to be the same situation the next time for anybody. It's going to be different. So, it's really the principle of it."

Skattebo, 24, leads the Giants with 496 yards rushing and four touchdowns on 116 carries so far this season.

Hutchinson, 26, isn't the first player to be injured while celebrating. Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL while celebrating a made kick against the Giants in 2001. But the current Hutchinson situation has prompted some debate about whether coaches should talk to players about celebrations, potentially banning anything that could be deemed dangerous.

"No, I don't believe that," Lions coach Dan Campbell said. "I think what happened speaks for itself. We're not talking to 8-year-olds here."

text:
After being placed on injured reserve for the second time this season earlier this month, San Francisco 49ers veteran wide receiver Christian Kirk won't be back on the field anytime soon.

Kirk posted a photo on Instagram revealing that he underwent meniscus surgery on his right knee. The post happened to be on his 30th birthday, and he wrote in the caption, "This year has been the hardest of my career."

After spending the previous three seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars, Kirk signed a one-year deal with the 49ers this past offseason. Unfortunately, his move to the Bay Area got off to a rocky start when he suffered a calf strain in training camp, forcing him to start the year on IR.

After being activated last month, Kirk appeared in just one game, failing to catch his lone target of the season in San Francisco's Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. He didn't see the field again before being placed on IR for the second time on Nov. 7 due to his knee injury.

Kirk's absence hasn't hurt the 49ers too much, as they have the best record in the NFC at 8-1 and the No. 1 offense in the league with 399.8 total yards per game. Star quarterback Brock Purdy has been stellar, completing 70.1 percent of his passes for 2,369 yards, 20 touchdowns and five interceptions. Star tight end George Kittle leads the team with 44 catches for 557 yards and five touchdowns.

With Kirk still on the mend, the 49ers will try to keep things rolling when they return to action in a marquee matchup against the Minnesota Vikings (7-2) on Sunday Night Football.

title: Week 11 Super Bowl stock report: Kirk Cousins raises Vikings' ceiling, Drake Maye injury ...
description:

Here are the latest trends in the Super Bowl race heading into Week 11.

text:
The first batch of NFL games after the trade deadline offered a first look at the teams that went all-in on a Super Bowl run. Although not all of the newcomers debuted with their squads — like the Jacksonville Jaguars' prized duo of Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III, who got a week off — some were tremendously impactful and proved their front offices right for investing in them.

Chief among those deadline acquisitions was Kirk Cousins. The Minnesota Vikings quarterback showed what is possible for the NFC North leaders when they have a functional offense.

At the same time that teams like the Vikings charged forward in the hunt for a championship, a couple of squads suffered devastating setbacks. In the Munich Game, both the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions suffered costly injuries that could make the difference in whether they can even compete for the Vince Lombardi Trophy.

This week's byes create the lightest slate of the year and give a handful of Super Bowl hopefuls a chance to recharge before the stretch run, but there are still a couple of contests on tap that should further shape the title picture.

Here are the latest trends in the Super Bowl race heading into Week 11.

Super Bowl odds entering Week 11

Odds via DraftKings, +2000 or better

49ers: +500

Bills: +500

Jaguars: +750

Bears: +850

Bengals: +950

Chiefs: +970

Rams: +1200

Seahawks: +1500

Vikings: +1500

Broncos: +1600

Lions: +1800

Stock up: Kirk Cousins raises Vikings' ceiling

Maybe the Vikings just have the Green Bay Packers' number this year, and it does not matter who lines up at quarterback. Heck, if Carson Wentz could defeat the division rivals by 17 points in the season opener, then there would have been no excuse for Cousins not to deliver a win, too, in Week 10. But maybe Cousins' arrival represents something far greater. For the first time since that first game of the season, Minnesota actually had life on offense. Its 30-10 win at Lambeau Field marked just its second 30-point game of the season.

If the offense simply stays out of the way, the Vikings are probably good enough to at least make the playoffs. If that unit is more than net neutral, though, this could become the best season in franchise history. The defense is that elite.

Nobody has scored more than 23 points on Brian Flores' defense all year. All Kevin O'Connell is asking of his offense is to score approximately that many of its own. A team that averages 23 points would rank 13th in the NFL in scoring. That is not an especially high bar. Cousins is enough of an upgrade over the situation Minnesota had at quarterback over the first two months of the year that he should be able to deliver that margin of improvement on his own.

A rejuvenated Justin Jefferson is a scary thing for opponents to see, and it is coming. He saw a season-high 13 targets in Cousins' debut and turned them into a 2026-best nine receptions. One that tandem fully rebuilds the connection that was so prolific during Cousins' first stint in Minnesota, teams will have to devote all kinds of resources to stopping him, which will open up other elements of the Vikings offense.

It is not often that a single player arrives as such an obvious savior in a team's pursuit of a championship. Cousins is exactly what the Vikings need.

With Kirk Cousins back, the Vikings really can win the Super Bowl and here's how

Ryan Wilson

Stock down: Drake Maye injury tanks Patriots

Injuries already accounted for a dip in Patriots stock prior to last week. The latest devastating one has New England's outlook at a new low.

The extent of Drake Maye's ankle injury is still to be announced, but the Patriots reportedly fear it is season-ending. Frankly, if Maye cannot play, New England's campaign is done. Tommy DeVito is not the caliber of backup who can step into action and shoulder the kind of load last year's MVP runner-up managed as the leader of an already banged-up unit. That much was clear when the offense sputtered in the 35-10 loss to the Lions in Germany.

It was always going to be an uphill battle for the Patriots to get back into the playoffs, let alone surge back to the Super Bowl, with the volume of absences that hit the offense. A.J. Brown's inability to get and stay healthy, Romeo Doubs' injured reserve stint, TreVeyon Henderson's illness, and a host of offensive line ailments forced this team to trudge through the mud even with Maye calling the shots. Losing the best and most important player in the group would be a death blow. And even if his ankle problem does not end his season, the hole he might find himself in when he returns to action will likely be too deep to climb out of.

Drake Maye injury the latest for Patriots amid snakebitten 2026 Super Bowl hangover

Tyler Sullivan

Long shot of the week: Panthers (+8000)

It is time to go back to the well for this week's top longshot. The flavor of the week in the NFC South tends to land here for one reason: none of the teams in this division are particularly good. Still, one of them has to make the playoffs and, by default, will finish the year no worse than four wins away from the Super Bowl. And since the Carolina Panthers are back in sole possession of first place, they are the pick for Week 11.

Standings aside, the Panthers are the team to back in the NFC South when it comes to projecting a division winner and one that could sneak its way to a win or two in the postseason. They forced the rest of the league to take them seriously last year when they nearly took down the Los Angeles Rams in the Wild Card round and have the upside to do something similar in 2026.

In addition to Bryce Young playing the best football of his career, the Panthers finally committed to Chuba Hubbard as a featured back this year, and the decision is paying dividends. He handled 27 of the team's 32 rushes in last week's critical win over the New Orleans Saints, finishing as the Panthers' leading rusher with 92 yards and two touchdowns and as their top receiver with five catches for 80 yards. His breakout season is a boon to an offense that occasionally shows flashes of excellence.

Perhaps even more important was the return of Jaelan Phillips. The Panthers went 0-3 without the edge rusher as he nursed a hamstring injury, but they are 4-2 with him in the lineup, and his sack and three tackles for loss against the Saints earned him NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors.

The Panthers are more "NFC South good" than "Super Bowl contender good," but as long as they win the division, they will have an opportunity to make noise in the postseason.

Week 10 games to watch

Vikings at 49ers

Sunday, 8:20 p.m., NBC, stream on Fubo (try for free)

This might be the game of the year in the NFC. The schematic matchup between Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores is bound to be one for the ages, and, not to be dramatic, but it might help determine how offenses and defenses attack each other in the years to come. Oh, and it is a clash between division leaders. This has "conference championship game preview" written all over it. How will Brock Purdy handle the Vikings' overwhelming pressure? Will Cousins and Jefferson continue to revitalize Minnesota's aerial attack? "Sunday Night Football" will bring answers and perhaps determine which of these teams is the deserving favorite to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl.

Jaguars at Giants

Sunday, 4:25 p.m., CBS, stream on Paramount+

Davis and Bates are set to make their Jacksonville debuts. The former will be tasked with containing Cam Skattebo, who has been on fire since his Oct. 18 benching with 243 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns in his last two games. The latter faces a New York Giants passing game that has been a pleasant surprise, with J.J. McCarthy outperforming expectations at quarterback. If the Jaguars are for real as the best team in the AFC, this is a game they win. But it is also a chance for the Giants to respond to their disappointing Week 10 loss and start rebuilding their NFC East lead.

Keeping players off the injury report has proved more difficult.

The Bills (8-1) have won five straight games and allowed just one touchdown over their last three. But several key contributors are dealing with injuries following Sunday's 31-12 victory over the New York Jets.

Benford suffered a groin injury against New York and was ruled out in the fourth quarter.

Williams suffered a calf injury in the fourth quarter against New York. He finished with a team-high nine tackles and his first career NFL sack.

Buffalo listed several players as limited participants, including safeties Cole Bishop (shoulder), Amani Hooker (knee) and Damar Hamlin (toe), running back Ray Davis (hamstring) and tight end Jackson Hawes (shoulder).

Wide receiver Keon Coleman (ankle), running back Ty Johnson (knee), center Connor McGovern (neck) and wide receiver Tyrell Shavers (knee) were full participants.

Miami had five players miss practice Wednesday, including starting center Aaron Brewer, who remains in concussion protocol. Backup center Andrew Meyer was limited with a neck injury.

title: Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) intends to play vs. Chargers: 'That's the plan' - ESPN
authors: Rich Cimini, David Purdum, David Schoenfield, Bradford Doolittle, Kiley McDaniel, Jorge Castillo, Jesse Rogers, ESPN staff, Tristan H. Cockcroft, Eric Karabell
description:

Smith was listed as a limited participant in practice -- not a regular practice, but an extensive walk-through, as the Jets like to call it.

text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- Quarterback Geno Smith still was walking with a noticeable limp Wednesday, three days after injuring his left ankle, but he intends to play Sunday when the New York Jets try to snap their five-game losing streak.

"That's the plan," Smith said. "Obviously, you've got to take it day by day, but that's the plan."

Smith was listed as a limited participant in practice -- not a regular practice, but an extensive walk-through, as the Jets like to call it. Barring a setback, he expects to face the Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) at SoFi Stadium.

"Yes, for sure," he said.

Embattled coach Aaron Glenn said he will let the week play out before announcing his plans. His options are a gimpy Smith or rookie Cade Klubnik, who replaced Smith in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills and was uneven in his NFL debut.

Glenn has made it clear that, even though the Jets are out of playoff contention with a 2-8 mark, he's not interested in turning the season over to the unproven Klubnik for evaluation purposes. Glenn, fighting for his job with a 5-22 record, said it would be "disrespectful" to bench Smith.

Smith has played reasonably well -- he's 19th in Total QBR (53.3) -- but the offense has gone nine straight quarters without a touchdown.

On Sunday, Smith was sidelined in the third quarter and never returned to the game. He went for a postgame X-ray and an MRI exam Monday, which showed no significant damage, a source said.

Smith wouldn't disclose the nature of the ankle injury, except to say it's "a little bit better [than Sunday]. I'm working through it." He took a few big hits in the game, acknowledging other aches and pains.

"Yeah, just working through some things, but just normal football stuff," he said.

When the starter is less than 100%, the distribution of practice reps can become an issue, especially if the backup is a rookie. Klubnik, who played only five series Sunday, had no practice reps with the starters before this week.

Glenn downplayed the matter, saying Klubnik will get a "fair amount of reps" in practice due to competition periods. In the game, the former Clemson star, a fourth-round pick, showed his inexperience. He led one field goal drive but also took three sacks and threw an interception. He completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards.

The sense in the locker room is that Smith will play.

title: NFL Fact Or Fiction: Burrow Over Allen, Purdy For MVP? Drew Lock Over Sam Darnold?
description:
Alright, let’s go: Fact or Fiction: Fiction Drew Lock has been fantastic this season!
Darnold has been inconsistent this season — he’s tied for the fifth-most interceptions (9) despite missing three games — but he’s been trying to find a rhythm through injury essentially all year.
Fact or Fiction: Fact The MVP race is long from over and Joe Burrow faces tight competition down the stretch from Bills QB Josh Allen, 49ers QB Brock Purdy and Packers QB Jordan Love, among others.
Fact or Fiction: Fiction I understand the thought process: The Vikings were essentially a quarterback away, and now they have … a quarterback.
Fact or Fiction: Fact Prospects look bleak for the Ravens right now, off the heels of an embarrassing loss to the Chargers.
text:
Do the defending-champion Seahawks have a quarterback controversy? Are the Ravens still a postseason contender despite losing to the previously winless Chargers? And who's most deserving to win NFL MVP this season?

I tackle those topics and more in the latest edition of "Fact or Fiction," where I hand out verdicts on fan takes sent to our @NFLonFOX Instagram each week.

Alright, let’s go:

Fact or Fiction: Fiction

Drew Lock has been fantastic this season! But I do think Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is right to continue rocking with Sam Darnold as QB1.

Darnold has been inconsistent this season — he’s tied for the fifth-most interceptions (9) despite missing three games — but he’s been trying to find a rhythm through injury essentially all year. He hurt his glute on the Seahawks’ fifth play of their opener against the Patriots, missing the rest of that game and the following week in the process. Then he played through a cracked rib in Week 8 against the Chicago Bears, against whom he suffered a quad injury that has forced him to miss the past two games.

Coming out of Seattle’s bye week, Darnold is expected to get a full week of practice ahead of the team’s Week 12 divisional showdown against the San Francisco 49ers. If you’re the Seahawks, I say you give him at least that game and the week following against the Cowboys’ (dreadful) defense to remind you that he’s the QB who led your team to the Super Bowl title last season.

If he doesn’t do that, well, you know you have a quarterback you can depend on in Lock, who’s 4-0 in games he’s appeared in this season. He’s completed 73.1% of his passes on the year for 837 yards and seven touchdowns with no interceptions and just five sacks. He’s lost two fumbles, but one of them was the result of running back Zach Charbonnet bumping into him while he was beginning a pass. So Lock has been playing at a high level.

His production could be a bit misleading, though. His four wins came against the Patriots, Cardinals (twice) and the Raiders. Arizona and Las Vegas are tied with the league-worst scoring defense (28.9 points per game allowed). New England is 17th in points allowed but has fallen apart recently, giving up 80 points over its past two games.

On the flip side, the past four defenses Darnold has faced all rank in the top 11 in scoring defense (49ers, Broncos, Chiefs, Bears). So that’s important context, too.

All that to say, Darnold should be safe as Seattle's QB1 … at least for now.

Fact or Fiction: Fact

The MVP race is long from over and Joe Burrow faces tight competition down the stretch from Bills QB Josh Allen, 49ers QB Brock Purdy and Packers QB Jordan Love, among others. But the Bengals quarterback is playing at a ridiculously high level, and it’s hard to imagine him slowing down … or slowing enough so that others can catch up to him.

He’s had five straight games with at least four offensive touchdowns, which ties Hall of Famer Peyton Manning’s 2004 league record, according to NFL research. It’s actually absurd how many categories Burrow leads the NFL in:

Completions (254)

Completion rate (74.7%)

Completion rate over expected (plus-7.4%)

Passing touchdowns (27)

First downs passing (142)

Passing success rate (57.6%)

Passing yards per game (310.6)

Passer rating (117.7) and

QBR (82.0)

He also ranks third in EPA per dropback (plus-.23) and fifth in yards per attempt (8.2).

From a team quality standpoint, Burrow’s MVP candidacy appears to be safe down the stretch. The Bengals (7-2) lead the AFC North and have a top-10 offense and defense through 10 weeks. And he has a great opportunity to continue padding his stats. Five of Cincinnati’s final eight games are against teams that rank in the bottom third of the league in scoring defense (Commanders, Saints, Panthers, Colts, Ravens).

So I really like Burrow’s odds of getting his first MVP award.

Fact or Fiction: Fiction

I understand the thought process: The Vikings were essentially a quarterback away, and now they have … a quarterback.

Acquired via trade from the Raiders days earlier, Kirk Cousins looked great in his first game back with Minnesota, throwing for 207 yards and two touchdowns with an interception to help the team to a blowout victory of the Packers — on the road against a division foe and fellow NFC contender.

The offense finally looks competent — the Vikings scored 30 points, their most since Week 1 — and Justin Jefferson had a season-high in catches (9) and targets (13) in the game, showing that Minnesota now has a pathway to keeping one of the NFL’s best wide receivers consistently involved.

All that is on top of a defense that is still elite. The Vikings held the Packers to 10 points last week, the seventh time this season that they’ve held their opponent under 20 points.

With all that said, though, it’s been just one game. Minnesota looks complete now on paper, but it needs to prove it for the long haul … in a way that the NFC-leading 49ers already have. The Bears are up there, too. One bad performance from QB Caleb Williams before Chicago’s bye (four interceptions) doesn’t take away from what the Bears are capable of as long as he’s healthy, and Williams is backed by the league’s No. 8 scoring defense.

I need to see more from the Vikings, specifically their offense. Yes, they scored 30 points last week with Cousins, but they also went 1-for-4 in the red zone. So there still needs to be consistency and growth from Minnesota on that side of the ball.

Fact or Fiction: Fact

Prospects look bleak for the Ravens right now, off the heels of an embarrassing loss to the Chargers. They’re on a five-game skid, tied for the longest in the NFL, but all hope shouldn’t be lost in Baltimore!

The Ravens are two games out of the final AFC wild-card spot with eight weeks left in the regular season, so there’s time. Their next three opponents are all below .500 — the Panthers (4-5), Texans (3-6) and Buccaneers (3-6).

Plus, despite the loss to the Chargers, the Ravens flashed competence on offense with Jacoby Brissett, acquired from the Arizona Cardinals before the trade deadline. With the veteran quarterback, Baltimore reached 20 points for the first time since Week 5 and registered a season-high in passing yards (331). The run game won’t look as bad as it did against the Chargers every week (16 net rushing yards). Brissett gives Baltimore a very real chance to stay competitive over the next month.

If two-time MVP Lamar Jackson returns from his thumb injury at the optimistic end of his recovery timeline, that puts him back around Week 16, when the Ravens host the Browns. Even if they lose to the Steelers the week prior, the Ravens will be in great shape in late December if they take care of business against the Panthers, Texans and Bucs.

text:
What happened to the Miami Dolphins and their defensive line over the past two weeks is completely ridiculous, and not in a good way.

And yet, they still rank in the middle of the pack when it comes to overall injury damage so far in the 2026 season.

Go figure.

According to the good folks over at Spotrac, the Dolphins are tied for 14th in the NFL with 10 players currently on IR after Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips joined Zach Sieler on Tuesday, and they're 22nd in terms of total weeks on IR with 58.

Those figures, of course, might be because before this trio of bad news, the Dolphins had been relatively spared from major injury news, at least comparatively speaking with the rest of the NFL.

Of course, it didn't help that one of the players the Dolphins lost early in the season to an injury was maybe their best player, that being running back De'Von Achane, but in terms of volume Miami was doing relatively well.

They certainly were nowhere near teams like the San Francisco 49ers (16 players, 139 total weeks) or the Detroit Lions (14 players, 105 weeks), who just watched their best defensive player tear an ACL after jumping to celebrate a sack.

The Dolphins actually were a lot more impacted by injuries in 2025 when they lost star wide receiver Tyreek Hill and starting guard James Daniels to season-ending injuries before the end of the first month and their final tally of 268 combined weeks on IR ranked third in the NFL behind the Arizona Cardinals' 315 and the 289 for the (them again) Lions.

THE D-TACKLE DEVASTATION FOR THE DOLPHINS

But that run of injuries at one position was just crazy, though.

It also might be worse because this was a position where the Dolphins had only four players on the roster before the run of bad luck began, with 2025 first-round pick Kenneth Grant now the only one of the bunch remaining.

Oh, and Grant was fourth at the position in terms of playing time.

Going back over the last 10 years, the only other instance where the Dolphins suffered that kind of concentration of injuries at one position came in 2019 — maybe not coincidentally the first year of the previous rebuilding project — when by November 20 they had lost three-fourths of their opening-day starter secondary.

On that November 2019 day, the Dolphins put cornerback Bobby McCain and safety Reshad Jones on injured reserve, where they joined cornerback Xavien Howard.

Going back further, we can look at the 2004 season when the Dolphins began the season with two run-stopping studs in the middle of the defensive line with Tim Bowens and Larry Chester, only to have Chester land on injured reserve after one game and Bowens join him after seven games.

Minus those two players, combined with a mediocre offense that didn't provide many leads, the Dolphins finished the season 31st in the NFL in rushing defense and had a 4-12 record.

The Dolphins actually were more decimated than that at linebacker in the 2023 season, though that run of bad luck happened late in the season when Jaelan Phillips, Bradley Chubb and Andrew Van Ginkel all went down. That left the Dolphins having to sign three free agents off the streets — Justin Houston, Bruce Irvin and Malik Reed — the week of their playoff game at Kansas City.

Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring.

The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter.

The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday.

As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign.

As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then.

The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.

Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee).

Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent.

While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety.

Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert.

Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck).

In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game.

The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin).

description:

text:
NEED TO KNOW

Travis Kelce considered whether the hit he took to his already-injured ankle on Sunday was intentional on Wednesday's episode of New Heights

His brother Jason Kelce said NFL players sometimes target opponents' known injuries during games

Kelce says he expects to play against the Arizona Cardinals as the Chiefs lead the AFC West

Travis Kelce is "ready to rock and roll" at the next Chiefs game despite the hit he absorbed on his already-injured ankle — a hit he acknowledges may have been intentional.

After the tight end, 37, was briefly knocked out of Kansas City's game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 15 with the hit, Kelce and his brother, Jason Kelce, debated on the Wednesday, Nov. 18 episode of their New Heights podcast whether the move was targeted.

Jason, 39, read off a question from a New Heights listener, who argued that Falcons safety DeMarcco Hellams made an "intentionally dirty tackle" targeting Travis' hurt ankle because the team knew from NFL injury reports that he already had a high-ankle sprain.

Travis, in response, hemmed over the question.

"I don't know if that was the case; the way he tackled me... and I just got caught in a bad position," the three-time Super Bowl champ said. "You know, that's football. And on the flip side, you know, if it was a quote-unquote intentional, you know, extra grab and turn of the ankle, you know, it's just part of it."

"I don't think it was, you know, crazy enough for it to get a flag or it to be a fine or anything like that," Travis continued. "Obviously, in the moment, I thought it was, because it hurt like hell."

VIPs Get More

Jason added that making injury reports more vague and keeping the information to just a lower-body or upper-body injury like in the NHL could help players stay healthy.

"It's an interesting point that Kyle is bringing up, because we do know that especially defensive players will target areas that they know are hurt," the retired Philadelphia Eagles star said. "If they know there's a knee injury, they're gonna go low. If they know, like, a quarterback has a specific hand that's hurt, they might go after the hand. Like, it's not like bounty gate-type stuff. It's just like a known thing that happens in the NFL."

Travis said, though, that he's feeling good ahead of the Chiefs' game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22..

"I'm ready to rock and roll this week," he said. "It's one of those things where once you turn it in at the beginning of the year, you've just got to deal with the high-ankle sprain and the process it takes to heal. When you're battling through week to week trying to get it to 100%, it's going to be a lot slower than just taking time off."

"But I love playing this game," he continued, "and if I'm out there on a good ankle or a bad ankle, it doesn't matter to me. I'm out there because I love this game. I signed up for this thing to be out there putting my heart on the line and my body on the line for my teammates."

Travis and the Chiefs improved to 7-2 after their dominant 35-10 win against the Falcons and have their minds set on winning a fourth Super Bowl in February.

"We're rolling," Travis said.

text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is done with his backflip touchdown celebration for the foreseeable future.

With Detroit Lions two-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffering a season-ending knee injury while jumping to celebrate a sack in Week 10, Skattebo is doing what he can to prevent suffering a similar fate as the 26-year-old edge rusher. That's why the backflips are on hiatus for the 24-year-old Giants running back.

"It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Wednesday, via ESPN. "I'm saying, yeah, [no backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That s--- ain't going to happen to me."

Despite suffering a serious, multi-faceted ankle injury in 2025, Skattebo returned to backflipping in 2026. He backflipped after a touchdown in the team's "Sunday Night Football" win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1, and he had multiple teammates joining him in backflipping in Week 10 on "Thursday Night Football" in a losing effort against the Washington Commanders.

He also backflipped after a 16-yard rushing touchdown against the Houston Texans in an overtime victory back in Week 7. However, he said the backflip could return ""if we go to the playoffs or something."

Hutchinson isn't the only NFL player to suffer a season-ending knee injury while celebrating. Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatic tore his ACL while celebrating a made field goal against the Giants in 2001. In baseball, Los Angeles Angeles first baseman/designated hitter Kendrys Morales suffered a leg and an ankle fracture while jumping on home plate after hitting a walk-off grand slam against the Seattle Mariners in 2010.

Skattebo, the Giants' leading rusher with 496 yards rushing and four rushing touchdowns on 116 carries in 2026, would be wise to heed those cautionary tales and celebrate touchdowns with his feet on the ground.

Wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. is also out with a hamstring for the second straight game.

On the Colts' side, they will be without Pro Bowl starting cornerback Charvarius Ward, who sustained a knee injury in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins and did not practice this week.

In the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston, Anderson dominated Indianapolis with 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He matched a career high with eight pressures in the game.

text:
The Houston Texans have released their third and final injury report of the week before they're tasked with a Thursday Night Football matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

And based on those newly-released statuses, the Texans will be without at least four players for Thursday's action, while also having a couple more names who are deemed questionable leading up to kickoff.

Let’s take a look at what both the Texans and Colts are dealing with in terms of injuries rolling into their primetime matchup for Week 11:

Houston Texans Injury Report (as of 11/18)

OUT

RB Woody Marks (concussion)

DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring)

WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring)

TE Brevin Jordan (foot/illness)

QUESTIONABLE

LB Jake Hummel (groin)

OL Wyatt Teller (back)

As for who will be out for the Texans, there's a couple of key starters that will miss out on the action and certainly shift the game plan from Houston's normal setup.

For one, the Texans will be without Danielle Hunter for a second straight game, as the veteran pass-rusher has been dealing with a lingering hamstring injury dating back to last week's practice before facing the Cleveland Browns.

This will mark his second-ever missed game while being a part of the Texans, as he's had a full 17-game attendance in both 2024 and 2025. Without Hunter, it likely means that Jadeveon Clowney will claim the vast majority of snaps as Houston's second edge rusher opposite of Will Anderson Jr., who doesn't have an injury designation like he did heading into Week 10.

The Texans will also be without their leader in the backfield from the past four weeks, Woody Marks, as he still remains in concussion protocol from last week's game against the Browns and will miss his first game of the regular season.

The good news for the Texans, though, is that they will be able to get David Montgomery back in the lineup, who's been stuck on the sidelines with a groin injury dating back to Week 5's game against the Tennessee Titans.

Montgomery should be expected to claim the bulk of Houston's carries on Thursday, while Emari Demercado operates as the Texans' RB2 as he has for the last two weeks since he's been signed to the active roster.

The Texans will also be without Marvin Harrison Jr. for a second straight game with a hamstring injury, while Brevin Jordan will be missing as well with a foot injury/illness.

That'll take two weapons away from C.J. Stroud's arsenal on Thursday, but leave him with a receiving corps still headlined by Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte.

Indianapolis Colts Injury Report (as of 11/18)

OUT

DT Jerry Tillery (calf)

OL Jalen Travis (knee)

CB Charvarius Ward (knee)

OL Bernhard Raimann (concussion)

TE Will Mallory (hamstring)

QUESTIONABLE

CB Sauce Gardner (calf)

WR Anthony Gould (toe)

OT Charlie Heck (personal)

LS Luke Rhodes (hamstring)

As for the injuries that the Colts will be dealing with on Thursday night, they won't be without their fair share of scratches as well.

And of the Colts' absences in Week 11, two names stick out a bit more than the rest: cornerback Charvarius Ward, who will be sidelined on Thursday due to a knee injury he was carted off from in last weekend's game against the Miami Dolphins, and starting left tackle Bernhard Raimann, who remains in concussion protocol.

Indianapolis might also have to go without their No. 1 corner, Sauce Gardner, who was listed as a DNP for all three days of the Colts' practice/walkthrough sessions, yet still seems to have his status left up in the air against the Texans.

If Gardner is forced out, that'll likely leave the Colts' primary slot corner, Justin Walley, as their primary boundary corner for the night, which was the role that he finished in at the end of Indianapolis' game against the Dolphins.

Kenneth Harris and Jonathan Edwards remain as their other two backup corners who could be set to see a bit more work in Week 11 with the injuries surfacing around the Colts' secondary, depending on what Gardner's status looks like closer to game time.

The Texans and Colts will kick off on Thursday Night Football at 7:15 p.m. CT, where a win for either side would mark their fourth on the season, and a big lift for their hopes of making a run within the second half of the regular season schedule.

John Mateer finished 21-of-33 for 207 yards and two touchdowns without an interception, adding another 56 yards on the ground in his first game under new play-caller Jason Witten. Oklahoma’s offense delivered when it mattered most, putting together an absolutely ridiculous 20-play, 89-yard drive that drained 12:45 off the clock before Isaiah Sategna III punched in a 6-yard touchdown. Mateer also connected with former Florida tight end Hayden Hansen for a score, adding a little extra insult to injury. But the defense stole the show.
